metadata.content: Thomas Tuchel: England manager faces pivotal international break to win over some players and supporters after World Cup exit | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Thomas Tuchel: England manager faces pivotal international break to win over some players and supporters after World Cup exit Thomas Tuchel must win over some England players and a large group of supporters who are still hurting from the World Cup defeat to Argentina; Tuchel still has the full support of the FA; England host Spain at Wembley in the Nations League on Saturday September 26 Rob Dorsett Football Correspondent @RobDorsettSky Thursday 17 September 2026 12:13, UK Image: Thomas Tuchel's England will face Spain, Czech Republic and Croatia in the Nations League Despite achieving England's best-ever World Cup performance on foreign soil, this international break feels like a pivotal moment in Thomas Tuchel's tenure. Tuchel signed a contract extension in February that will take him through Euro 2028, and he still has the full support of his bosses at the Football Association. The governing body is still conducting a full review of England's 2026 World Cup, which is standard practice after every major competition, but it is understood that, overall, his bosses have deemed the third-placed finish a success. messages.text: Carrick, INEOS, defence... what is behind Man Utd's latest problems?

metadata.summary: Manchester United's collapse against Brighton has intensified the scrutiny on Michael Carrick - but the problems at Old Trafford run deeper than the head coach.
metadata.content: Manchester United: What's to blame for latest problems and results increasing scrutiny on Michael Carrick after Carabao Cup exit? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Manchester United: What's to blame for latest problems and results increasing scrutiny on Michael Carrick after Carabao Cup exit? Michael Carrick is under increasing scrutiny at Manchester United; Man Utd have crashed out of the Carabao Cup and have produced their joint-worst start to a Premier League season; Vote on what you think the main issue is at Old Trafford below William Bitibiri Football Journalist @williambitibiri Thursday 17 September 2026 14:17, UK Image: What is is the biggest issue at Manchester United? Manchester United's collapse against Brighton has intensified the scrutiny on Michael Carrick - but the problems at Old Trafford run deeper than the head coach. United led 2-0 after just 10 minutes against Brighton on Wednesday night. By full-time, they had lost 3-2, exited the Carabao Cup at the third-round stage for a second successive season and been booed off by their own supporters. It was the first time in 50 years United had lost at Old Trafford after going 2-0 up. They had won 143 of the previous 145 matches in which they had established that advantage. They also failed to register another shot on target after Mason Mount's 2-0 goal until the 76th minute. messages.text: 'Man City are not champions' - Why Greenwood's claim should scare rivals

metadata.summary: Manchester City have set their stall out scarily early. Captain Alex Greenwood did so in pre-season. "A true champion is someone who goes and wins again. A winner might be one-off. But a champion does it over and over."
metadata.content: Man City vs Liverpool: Why graduating from WSL winner to champion is so important to Alex Greenwood | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Man City vs Liverpool: Why graduating from WSL winner to champion is so important to Alex Greenwood In conversation with Sky Sports before the start of the season, Man City captain Alex Greenwood explains her desire to lead a team of champions - not just winners; watch Man City vs Liverpool live on Sky Sports+ on Friday; kick-off 7pm Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Wednesday 16 September 2026 08:48, UK Image: Alex Greenwood captained Manchester City to a historic WSL and FA Cup double in the 2025/26 season Manchester City have set their stall out scarily early. Captain Alex Greenwood did so in pre-season. "A true champion is someone who goes and wins again. A winner might be one-off. But a champion does it over and over." Beginning the new campaign with back-to-back victories - the only team to do so - is testament to Greenwood's belief that there is a clear distinction between being a winner and being a champion. Becoming a champion is a process of progression, one that can only be achieved by consistently backing up what has already been accomplished. Only one side has maximum points after the first two match rounds of this term, something that has not happened since 2015.
